name: Paracetamol
summary: A central analgesic for pain and fever that is not a classic NSAID, so it avoids the strong COX-1 GI tradeoff seen with ibuprofen or naproxen.
good: Mild to moderate pain or fever when GI or renal risk makes NSAIDs undesirable.
bad: Severe inflammatory pain where a true anti-inflammatory effect is needed, or any setting with possible overdose risk.
clinicalPearls: It is often the safest first step for simple pain, but the safety margin collapses once the dose creeps up repeatedly.
mechanism: Primarily central analgesia and antipyresis; it weakly affects peripheral prostaglandin pathways and is not a strong anti-inflammatory drug.
indications: Fever, headache, dental pain, musculoskeletal aches, and first-line symptomatic relief when GI risk makes NSAIDs less attractive.
interactionNotes: Alcohol misuse, other hepatotoxic drugs, and combination cold products can all push the total daily dose into unsafe territory.

warnings: Overdose can cause severe hepatotoxicity; dose discipline matters more than perceived gentleness.
